title: GenAI / Agentic AI Security Incident
description: Schema for a single incident entry in the genai_incidents dataset, a consolidated index of GenAI and agentic AI security incidents. Every entry is mapped to four core taxonomies (OWASP LLM Top 10, OWASP Agentic (ASI) Top 10, NIST AI RMF, MITRE ATLAS) where applicable, plus optional companion MAESTRO and experimental VERIS crosswalk fields.

source_ids.description: Upstream identifiers when consolidated from external sources (e.g. AIID-123, CVE-2025-xxxxx, ATLAS-AML.CS0001, AVID-2024-V005)

cwe_ids.description: Common Weakness Enumeration identifiers (e.g. CWE-79, CWE-918).

capec_ids.description: MITRE CAPEC attack-pattern identifiers, derived from the entry's CWEs via the authoritative CWE->CAPEC map (mappings/cwe_capec.json). A complete (uncapped) denormalisation — see DATA_DICTIONARY.md.

purl.description: Package-URLs (purl, pkg:type/namespace/name) derived from structured GHSA/OSV `affected` identifiers — entity-resolution anchors for affected packages. See DATA_DICTIONARY.md.

exploited_in_wild.description: True when one of the entry's CVEs appears in the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog.

kev_date_added.description: Earliest date the entry's CVE(s) were added to the CISA KEV catalog.

aiid_id.description: Canonical AI Incident Database numeric ID where this entry has an AIID counterpart.

disclosure_date.description: Public disclosure date when distinct from the incident date.

date.description: ISO date, year-only, or year-month allowed

description.description: Free text aggregated verbatim from upstream advisories. UNTRUSTED: may contain raw HTML / exploit payloads (e.g. '') from the original write-ups. Consumers MUST escape/sanitize before rendering it as HTML or Markdown.

description_provenance.description: Provenance of the current description field's content. verbatim = copied unmodified from an upstream source. summary = model-assisted paraphrase of upstream prose, pre-generated offline and committed under data/summaries/, never generated during make build. original = independently composed from facts/metadata, not a paraphrase of any single upstream source's prose. Absence means not yet assessed.

description_source.description: Short slug naming which upstream ingest contributed the CURRENT description field's content (e.g. aiaaic), meaningful only when description_provenance is set. Needed because description (and this field) are set once by whichever entry survives dedup as the merge target and are never overwritten by later merges, unlike source_ids and tags which merge/union across every absorbed duplicate.

content_license.description: Row-level license-obligation marker: this entry's CONTENT derives from an upstream source whose license imposes obligations (attribution, possibly share-alike) on the row itself, over and above the repository's own LICENSE-DATA. Source-generic by design — the source is named in the `source` VALUE, never in the field name, so any future source with row-level obligations reuses this mechanism unchanged. Set at ingest, by whichever entry survives dedup as the merge target. Historically set in lockstep with `description_source` for AIAAIC-sheet rows (both provenance fields describe the same aiaaic-origin description); since 2026-07-29 (E16/D18) also set independently on the 95 hand-curated AIAAIC rows, whose title (and, before retitling, in 13 cases the title verbatim) derives from AIAAIC even though their `description` is project-authored and carries no `description_source`. `content_license` and `description_source` are two independent per-field provenance markers that happen to coincide on sheet-derived rows, not one joint marker. Like description_source it is EXCLUDED from merge_into's union/absorb behaviour (that exclusion is what keeps it sticky and truthful) and is never overwritten by a later merge. Surfaces: data/incidents.json and the HuggingFace export carry it in full; data/incidents.min.json carries it on marked rows only, absent elsewhere; the STIX bundle mirrors it per-row as an `x_content_license` custom property (D14), emitted from this field verbatim; the interim pre-rebuild AIAAIC-source heuristic that stood in for it before the field was populated was retired at D15 (2026-07-29), once the field was confirmed to match the heuristic's output exactly on every affected row with zero divergence in either direction; MISP carries no description at all and so no marker (D12(b), as revised by D14). Absence means no row-level obligation is known for this entry — NOT that the entry is unencumbered.

source.description: Slug of the upstream source imposing the obligation, drawn from the same vocabulary as description_source (e.g. aiaaic). The obligation is source-specific; the mechanism is not.

license.description: SPDX license identifier of the upstream content license, e.g. CC-BY-SA-4.0.

license_url.description: Canonical URL of the license deed or legal code. Supply it wherever the license has a stable public URL: a consumer holding only incidents.min.json may see no other license surface.

attribution.description: Human-readable attribution target — the party to credit under the license's attribution clause, e.g. 'AIAAIC Repository'.

attribution_url.description: URL to credit alongside attribution. Optional: not every source publishes a stable one.

obligations.description: Which obligations actually attach to this row, stated explicitly rather than inferred from `license`, so that a later waiver or narrowing by the source downgrades a VALUE (drop 'share-alike') instead of changing the field's shape.

attack_vector.description: Primary attack mechanism — free-form but should match one of the controlled values where possible.

affected.description: Vendor, product, organization, or system affected

reversibility_class.description: Reversibility of the action that closed the incident (#74), ordered least→most severe: read-only = no state mutation; reversible = undoable in-session or by trivial in-system action; external-reversible = undoable only via an external compensating action (refund, retraction, cleanup); irreversible = no compensating action possible. Landmark-tier only, assigned via data/curation_overrides.json where source evidence describes the closing action. Absent = unassessed, NOT read-only. The enum carries no lexical order — consumers must rank explicitly.

discovery_method.description: How the incident was first surfaced (lineage: VERIS 1.4.1 discovery_method, flattened and AI-adapted; media-report has no VERIS parent). Landmark-tier only, assigned via data/curation_overrides.json where the source states the discovery channel — same evidence-gated mechanism as reversibility_class (#74). Absent = unassessed, NOT internally detected.

quality_tier.description: How well-vetted the entry is. `curated` = hand-written or maintainer-reviewed; `reviewed` = sourced from a maintained research catalogue; `auto` = bulk-ingested.

confidence.description: Transparent, rule-derived confidence in the entry (see DATA_DICTIONARY.md). high = curated/reviewed OR 2+ distinct sources with a CVE; medium = 2+ sources OR has a CVE/CVSS; low = a single auto-tier source.

tier.description: Curated/notable `landmark` incidents vs the comprehensive vulnerability/advisory `feed`. DERIVED — recomputed from scratch on every build by `scripts/merge_and_dedupe.py::_derive_tier`, which is the only definition of record: `landmark` iff `quality_tier == "curated"` OR `aiid_id` is present OR `corpus == "ai-harm"`; everything else is `feed`. Two corrections landed here on 2026-09-18 (WS6-T9), both because this description is what README points readers to. (1) The clause `or real-world-category` was removed: the `category == "real-world"` criterion was dropped from the code before #68 merged, because it also tags exploited CVEs — read literally, the old wording described roughly 3.6x the rows the code actually marks, and it said so for three months. (2) The cross-reference to INCLUSION.md §5 was removed: §5 describes the split in terms of `quality_tier` (curated/reviewed vs auto), which is a DIFFERENT axis and a different set — reconciling §5's prose to this derivation is an open item for the maintainer, so until it closes this field's definition is the code, not §5. `tier` is NOT recoverable from `quality_tier`: the majority of landmark rows are landmark only by `aiid_id`, and `aiid_id` and `quality_tier` disagree by design. Because the published landmark count is the figure README tells consumers to cite, this field is carried by EVERY distributed variant — full JSON, `incidents.min.json` and its site/PyPI copies, the site core bundle, the Hugging Face export, STIX as `x_tier`, MISP as a `genai-incidents:tier` tag — so that count is reproducible from any artifact we ship, not just from the full file. `tests/test_landmark_distribution.py` is the gate on that. Cite the landmark count for headlines.

source_count.description: Number of distinct upstream sources (source_ids) corroborating the entry.

source_status.description: EMISSION status, not liveness status. Whether the entry is still emitted by at least one source on the latest build (`active`) or was retained from a prior build after all its sources dropped it (`retained`). Read the sentence a consumer will actually form, and reject it: `active` does NOT mean the upstream source is still alive or still being refreshed successfully. It means only that the entry appeared in this build's inputs — and an ingest snapshot committed to the repository re-emits its rows on every build whether or not the source that produced it still exists. That misreading is what let 1,380 AIRI-derived rows read as current for the seven weeks after that source's last successful refresh on 2026-05-31, without any field in the data being false. Source FRESHNESS is a separate, independent axis: published per source in data/source_freshness.json and surfaced per row as `source_freshness`. The two combine freely — an entry can be active-and-fresh, active-and-stale, retained-and-fresh, or retained-and-stale — which is why freshness is not, and must not become, a third value of this enum.

source_freshness.description: Derived per-row projection of data/source_freshness.json: at least one source that contributed to this entry has stopped refreshing successfully, so part of this entry's content is current only up to `as_of`. Inherited BY REFERENCE, never authored per row — every value here is reconstructable from the registry plus the entry's source tags, and each `sources` element is a key into the registry's `sources` object where the full source-level record (label, stale_since, hold, notes) lives. Emitted ONLY on entries with at least one `stale` contributing source; its ABSENCE means no contributing source is currently registered stale — NOT that the entry is verified current, and NOT that its sources are tracked at all (data/source_freshness.json `coverage` names the ingests nothing measures). Independent of `source_status`, which is an emission status; see that field. Deliberately self-sufficient — status, date and source keys are all inline — so a consumer holding only incidents.min.json or the HuggingFace projection can read it without joining to the registry.

status.description: Single-valued today, and that is a decision rather than an oversight: the registry's `degraded` state (a source that failed below the consecutive-failure threshold) deliberately does NOT propagate here, because a transient blip would otherwise add and remove this field across thousands of rows on a flaky week and make the field's own churn unreadable. The threshold already exists to separate a hiccup from a death; this reuses it. Extending the enum to `degraded` is a value change, not a shape change.

as_of.description: The date through which this entry's content from the listed sources is current — the EARLIEST `last_success` among them, so a row fed by two stale sources reports the more conservative date. Says nothing about content the entry received from sources that are still fresh.

sources.description: Sorted, unique keys into data/source_freshness.json `sources` — exactly the contributing sources that are stale, never the entry's full source set. A cross-listed entry whose other sources are healthy lists only the stale one, because that is the true claim: part of this row is old, not all of it.

first_seen.description: Date the entry first entered the dataset (provenance alias of `added`).

last_seen.description: Date the entry's content was last confirmed/updated from a source (provenance alias of `updated`).

corpus.description: Which sub-corpus the entry belongs to. `security` = exploitation, vulnerability, misuse; `ai-harm` = bias/discrimination/social harm without a security primitive.

owasp_llm.description: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications (2026) codes

owasp_dsgai.description: OWASP Data Security for GenAI codes (legacy/companion)

added.description: Date this entry was first added to the dataset

allOf.$comment: Row-level license obligations are per-source. Every entry whose `description_source` is `aiaaic` must also carry `content_license` (enforced below) — that direction still holds. The converse does not: since E16/D18 (2026-07-29), the 95 hand-curated AIAAIC rows also carry `content_license` via their AIAAIC-sourced title/facts, even though their `description` is project-authored and carries no `description_source`. When another source acquires row-level obligations, extend the conditional per source — re-scope it, never drop it.
